ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a regular hexagon and a square located in the same plane, and the bottom side of the square coincides with one side of the regular hexagon. ∠1 is marked at the right endpoint of this common side, located between the right side of the square and the adjacent slanted side of the regular hexagon. Reasoning: Because both figures are regular polygons, the interior angle of the regular hexagon is (6-2)×180°/6=120°, and the interior angle of the square is (4-2)×180°/4=90°. At the common endpoint, ∠1 is the angle remaining after removing the interior angle of the square from the interior angle of the regular hexagon, so ∠1=120°-90°=30°.

method.method_draft: Read from the image: the regular hexagon and the square share one side, and angle 1 is the open angle at their common endpoint between the square’s side and the adjacent side of the hexagon. Read from the text: both shapes are regular, so their interior angles are fixed. Bridge: compute each polygon’s interior angle and subtract at the shared vertex. A regular hexagon has interior angle (6-2)×180°/6=120°, and a square has interior angle (4-2)×180°/4=90°. The marked angle is the difference 120°-90°=30°.
